Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctu.ref: Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctuary 3:13
Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctu.he: וְאֵי זֶהוּ הַטָּמֵא שֶׁחַיָּב כָּרֵת עַל הַמִּקְדָּשׁ כָּל שֶׁנִּטְמָא בְּטֻמְאָה מִן הַמֵּת שֶׁהַנָּזִיר מְגַלֵּחַ עָלֶיהָ שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְפָּרֵשׁ בִּנְזִירוּת. אוֹ שֶׁיִּגַּע בָּאָדָם אוֹ בְּכֵלִים שֶׁנִּטְמְאוּ בְּאוֹתָן הַטֻּמְאוֹת שֶׁהַנָּזִיר מְגַלֵּחַ עֲלֵיהֶם שֶׁהֲרֵי הוּא שֵׁנִי לָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנָּגַע בְּמֵת. אוֹ שֶׁנִּטְמָא בִּשְׁאָר אֲבוֹת הַטֻּמְאוֹת שֶׁל תּוֹרָה שֶׁיִּתְפָּרְשׁוּ בִּמְקוֹמָן:
Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctu.en:
What are the types of impurity for which one is liable [for entering] the Temple [while impure]?
a) Anyone who became impure through contact with a human corpse in a manner which would require a nazirite to shave [his head] because of them; these are explained in [Hilchot] Nizirut;
b) one who touched a person or a utensil that became impure through those types of impurity for which a nazirite must shave [his head]; for such a person is considered as a second level of impurity to a primary object of impurity that touched a corpse;
c) one who became impure through contact with another primary source of impurity as mandated by Scriptural Law, as will be explained in their appropriate places.
Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctu.heRef: משנה תורה, הלכות ביאת מקדש ג׳:י״ג

Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctu.ref: Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctuary 3:15
Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctu.he: וְכֵן הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּכֵלִים שֶׁנָּגְעוּ בְּאָדָם שֶׁנָּגַע בְּמֵת אוֹ שֶׁנָּגַע בְּאָדָם שֶׁנָּגַע בְּכֵלִים הַנּוֹגְעִים בְּמֵת אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא רִאשׁוֹן לְעִנְיַן תְּרוּמָה וּלְטַמֵּא בְּשַׂר קָדָשִׁים הֲרֵי זֶה פָּטוּר עַל בִּיאַת הַמִּקְדָּשׁ. שֶׁדְּבָרִים אֵלּוּ הֲלָכָה מִפִּי הַקַּבָּלָה. וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא פָּטוּר מַכִּין אוֹתוֹ מַכַּת מַרְדּוּת:
Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctu.en: Similarly, if one touches utensils that touched a human corpse or touches a person who is touching utensils that touch a corpse, even though he is considered as impure to the first degree with regard to terumah and with regard to imparting impurity to sacrificial foods, he is exempt for entering the Temple. For these matters are laws received through the Oral Tradition. Although he is exempt, he is given stripes for rebellious conduct.
Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctu.heRef: משנה תורה, הלכות ביאת מקדש ג׳:ט״ו

Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctu.ref: Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctuary 3:17
Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctu.he: יֵרָאֶה לִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה אֶלָּא עַל בְּגָדִים שֶׁהֵן אַב טֻמְאָה. כְּגוֹן בְּגָדִים שֶׁנָּגַע בָּהֶן זֶה הַטָּמֵא לְמֵת שֶׁהֵן אַב הַטֻּמְאָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּתְבָּאֵר. אֲבָל בֶּגֶד שֶׁהוּא רִאשׁוֹן אִם הִכְנִיסוֹ לַמִּקְדָּשׁ אֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה עָלָיו אֲבָל מַכִּין אוֹתוֹ מַכַּת מַרְדּוּת:
Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctu.en: It appears to me that he is liable for lashes only for his clothes that are a source of ritual impurity, i.e., clothes that were touched by a person who became impure through contact with a corpse that themselves become a source for ritual impurity, as will be explained. If, by contrast, one brings a garment which is of first degree impurity into the Temple, he is not liable for lashes. He does, however, receive stripes for rebellious conduct.
Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctu.heRef: משנה תורה, הלכות ביאת מקדש ג׳:י״ז

Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctu.ref: Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctuary 3:3
Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctu.he: וּמְשַׁלְּחִין זָבִין וְזָבוֹת נִדּוֹת וְיוֹלְדוֹת חוּץ לִשְׁתֵּי מַחֲנוֹת שֶׁהוּא חוּץ לְהַר הַבַּיִת. מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מְטַמְּאִין הַמִּשְׁכָּב וְהַמּוֹשָׁב אֲפִלּוּ מִתַּחַת הָאֶבֶן מַה שֶּׁאֵין הַמֵּת מְטַמֵּא:
Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctu.en: Men with a zav condition, women with a zavah condition, niddot, and women who gave birth are sent outside two camps, i.e., outside the Temple Mount. [The rationale for this severity is that] they cause an entity upon which they are seated or upon which they are lying to become ritually impure, even if it is under a stone. [This does not apply] with regard to impurity [contracted] from a corpse.
Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctu.heRef: משנה תורה, הלכות ביאת מקדש ג׳:ג׳

Mishneh Torah, Defilement by Leprosy 10:.he: הַמְצֹרָע אָב מֵאֲבוֹת הַטֻּמְאוֹת מְטַמֵּא אָדָם וְכֵלִים בְּמַגָּעוֹ וּכְלֵי חֶרֶס בַּאֲוִירוֹ וּמְטַמֵּא אָדָם בְּמַשָּׂא וּמְטַמֵּא מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב אֲפִלּוּ תַּחַת אֶבֶן כְּזָב וּכְזָבָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר <small>(ויקרא יג ו)</small> "וְכִבֶּס בְּגָדָיו וְטָהֵר" מִפִּי הַשְּׁמוּעָה לָמְדוּ שֶׁטָּהֵר מִלְּטַמֵּא מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב. וְאֶחָד הַמֻּסְגָּר וְאַחַד הַמֻּחְלָט בְּכָל אֵלּוּ:
Mishneh Torah, Defilement by Leprosy 10:.en: A person afflicted with tzara'at is a primary source of impurity. He imparts impurity to humans and implements through touching them and to earthenware containers when a portion of his body enters their inner space. He imparts impurity to a person when carried by him and an object over which he lies or sits even if there is a stone intervening between him and their surface, as is the law regarding a zav and a zavah. This is derived from Leviticus 13:6: "He shall launder his garments." According to the Oral Tradition, it was taught that he becomes pure with regard to imparting impurity to the objects on which he lies or sits. All of these laws apply equally to one isolated because of tzara'at and one deemed definitively impure].
Mishneh Torah, Defilement by Leprosy 10:.heRef: משנה תורה, הלכות טומאת צרעת י׳:י״א

Mishneh Torah, Defilement by a Corpse 1:.ref: Mishneh Torah, Defilement by a Corpse 1:5
Mishneh Torah, Defilement by a Corpse 1:.he: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאָדָם מִתְטַמֵּא בִּנְגִיעָתוֹ בְּטֻמְאָה כָּךְ הַכֵּלִים מִתְטַמְּאִים בִּנְגִיעַת הַטֻּמְאָה בָּהֶן. חוּץ מִכְּלִי חֶרֶס שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְטַמֵּא אֶלָּא מֵאֲוִירוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּתְבָּאֵר בְּהִלְכוֹת כֵּלִים. [וְזֶהוּ כְּלָל גָּדוֹל בַּטֻּמְאָה. כָּל הַמְטַמֵּא אָדָם בְּמַגָּע מְטַמֵּא כֵּלִים. וְכָל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא אָדָם בְּמַגָּע אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא כֵּלִים. וְאֵין אָדָם וְכֵלִים מְקַבְּלִין טֻמְאָה אֶלָּא מֵאַב הַטֻּמְאָה]:
Mishneh Torah, Defilement by a Corpse 1:.en:
Just as a person becomes impure when he comes into contact with a source of impurity, so too, keilim become impure when a source of impurity touches them with the exception of an earthenware utensil that incurs ritual impurity only when a source of impurity enters its inner space, as will be explained in Hilchot Keilim.
This is an inclusive general principle that applies with regard to ritual impurity: Whatever causes a person to contract ritual impurity when touching him, causes keilim to contract ritual impurity. Whatever does not cause a person to contract ritual impurity when touching him, does not cause keilim to contract ritual impurity. A person and keilim contract ritual impurity only from a primary source of ritual impurity.
Mishneh Torah, Defilement by a Corpse 1:.heRef: משנה תורה, הלכות טומאת מת א׳:ה׳
